Folks — forwarding Acme's ask. Quick proposal below that I will turn into a one-page verification matrix (rid-validation-matrix-v1.xlsx) and share with Acme by EOD. Please flag any technical or commercial concerns.

Proposed phased schedule (high level):
1) Baseline characterization (day 0–1): scoped load tests against their representative model variant using Acme's traffic profile (no customer traffic impacted).
2) Performance validation (day 2–3): sustained run at 70% of expected committed throughput; measure latency P50/P95, token cost per 1k, and OOM/retry behavior. Acceptance gate: P95 within agreed SLA band or documented trade-offs.
3) Rehearsal (day 6): live canary with 5% production traffic routed to dedicated pool for a 3-hour window; observe KV-cache warmup and steady-state throughput.
4) Swap window (day 7): 60-minute cutover window with a 15-minute rollback gate. Pre-cutover checklist + post-cutover sanity checks.

Operational notes:
- We should include an explicit cache-warmup script during rehearsal (Jordan to draft).
- Marcus: confirm GPU instance sizing and whether we need an extra spare node for the rehearsal.
- Karthik: validate that quantized model variant is available on the dedicated runtime; if not, list the expected delta.

I'll attach the validation matrix draft and send to Acme.

Neha Kapoor
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

+1 to Neha's plan. A few technical clarifications and asks:

- Model variant: Acme's ingest shows ~70% of requests use the long-context route (~2k tokens). The dedicated runtime should be preloaded with the float16 variant; if they require int8 quant, we need 24–36 hours for conversion and a quick perf smoke.
- GPU sizing: based on the profile file, I'd suggest an initial pool of 6 A100-equivalent slots with 2 spare warm nodes for rehearsal. Marcus, please confirm memory headroom.
- KV-cache warmup: recommend a 6-hour synthetic warmup run that mimics their top 20 prefixes (Jordan to collect top prefixes). This prevents an artificial P95 spike on cutover.
- Monitoring: add token-level cost telemetry to the rehearsal so we can compare with hosted baseline (we'll need a short snippet to map token counts to billable units).

I'll update the matrix with these items. If Acme wants to shorten to a 4-hour rehearsal, call that out as a risk.

Karthik
Director, Serving & Runtime

Confirmed dates (proposed):
- Warmup job: June 3, 2028, 08:00–14:00 PST (6-hour synthetic warmup beginning 08:00; extra buffer until 14:00 for observation).
- Performance validation run: June 4, 2028, 09:00–12:00 PST (sustained run at 70% throughput).
- Rehearsal (canary): June 6, 2028, 09:00–12:00 PST (5% live traffic routed; 3-hour observation window).
- Cutover window: June 7, 2028, 10:00–11:00 PST (60-minute swap; rollback gate at 10:15 if P95 > agreed threshold or error rate increases > 0.5%).

Rollback and acceptance gates (short):
- Rollback triggers: P95 latency > SLA threshold by > 20% for two consecutive 5-minute buckets OR error rate (5xx) increases by > 0.5% baseline for 10 minutes.
- Acceptance: P95 within SLA band OR documented trade-off accepted and signed by Acme ops + Redwood on the SOW.

Operational owners:
- Redwood runtime: Karthik (exec), Marcus (infra lead), Jordan (cutover runbook).
- Acme on-call: Elaine (ops), procurement for PO + final signatures.
